$comment: GARDEN-ONLY portability rules, layered on top of the CANONICAL parity fixture tests/portability_rules.json (vendored byte-for-byte from wicked-crew packages/crew/tests/fixtures/portability_rules.json — never edit that file here; re-vendor it and update tests/test_portability_fixture_parity.py). The shared tokens (plugin-root, skill-dir-var, cwd-script, relative-link, cross-skill-path, requires-harness:claude) and ALL their semantics — regexes, fence walk, option skipping, existence, ../ resolution — live only in the canonical file and are derived by the same engine crew uses. This file holds what garden's authoring convention adds on top: the exact `## Runtime` block, the name-based cross-ref resolver, the slash-form ban, the bare-script-span extension of cwd-script, the stricter bare-identifier check, the `verdict-spelling` grammar, and — since L6 B0 (D-21, cross-CLI skill format, docs/cross-cli-skill-format.md) — the seven cross-CLI tokens whose HEAD hits are BASELINED per (token, file) in tests/cross_cli_baseline.json until the qe batches translate each skill (a stale entry fails; B18 deletes the file). The former Claude-first fallback sentences (fork-no-fallback / dispatch-no-fallback / ask-no-fallback) are retired: the Claude shape itself is the finding now. Regexes stay in the ECMAScript/Python common subset.

launcher.runtime_block:
## Runtime
Script-backed steps use the `wicked-garden` launcher: `wicked-garden run <plugin-root-relative path, e.g. scripts/…> [args]`. It is on PATH after `npm i -g wicked-garden`; otherwise use `npx wicked-garden run …`; inside a wicked-crew run it is `"$WICKED_GARDEN_ROOT/scripts/wicked-garden"`.
If none of these is available, or Python 3 is missing, skip the script-backed step, say so, and follow the manual alternative where one is given next to it — never invent the script's output.
Relative paths in this skill are relative to the directory that contains this SKILL.md.

skill_names.exemption_marker_scope: token: the marker must directly follow the wicked-garden-<x> token (an optional closing quote/backtick and spaces may sit between); a marker elsewhere on the line exempts nothing

cross_cli.$comment: The eight cross-CLI tokens (L6 B0; claude-tool-call added by the B7 fold, review-garden-1153 M1). Detectors run over every skills/**/*.md body (frontmatter tokens over SKILL.md frontmatter); a line carrying historical_marker is never a hit; prose inside a Hand-off paragraph (a paragraph whose first line matches handoff_regex) is exempt from claude-only-prose — the Hand-off paragraph is the ONE cross-CLI dispatch shape. closed_frontmatter_keys mirrors scripts/_skill_meta.CLOSED_KEYS (the test pins the two equal).

verdict_spelling.$comment: verdict-spelling (FIX-IT-ALL L6-0, D-9 text half). wicked-core's evaluator gate reads the LAST line of an evaluator unit's output matching regex.verdict_line and passes ONLY on the token PASS; every other token or a missing line parks the run at the human gate. Garden text therefore asks for nothing but the two spellings (or the template) on such a line. legacy_footer_files: qe specialists still carrying the pre-12.37 `VERDICT=PASS|FAIL|{PASS|FAIL} REVIEWER=… RUN_ID=…` footer — it parses as PASS/FAIL so it is tolerated THERE ONLY; the qe batches (B14-B17) rewrite each footer to the grammar and delete its entry in the same change, and a listed file with no footer left fails tests/test_skill_portability.py (stale baseline). Never add a file here to silence the lint.

codemod.note: the codemod (scripts/wg/portability_codemod.py, dev tooling) rewrites MORE than the lint judges — yaml/yml fences too, since a CI template's `run:` lines are shell — rewriting toward the launcher is always safe

tokens.garden_extension: garden also fails on the bare identifier CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT anywhere under skills/ (crew: the `${…}` marker only)
garden also fails on the bare identifier CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR

a bare `scripts/<x>.py <args>` code span, or a shell-fence line that starts with such a path and is not a `\` continuation, with no interpreter at all — an instruction no host can execute — when the path exists at the plugin root and not inside the referencing skill

tokens.rule: a wicked-garden-<x> name (prose, .md files) that no SKILL.md declares; template forms (`{`, or followed by `-` as in wicked-garden-qe-{a, b} / wicked-garden-qe-* / wicked-garden-<x>) are skipped; the inline marker `<!-- not-a-skill -->` placed DIRECTLY AFTER a token (`wicked-garden-x` <!-- not-a-skill -->) declares that token an identifier (an evaluator id, a sibling plugin), not a cross-ref — the design scopes this token to dispatch/cross-refs and the marker keeps that declaration next to the text instead of in a central allowlist (which stays empty)
a skill whose own files use `wicked-garden run|python|path` must carry the exact ## Runtime block in its SKILL.md
a /wicked-garden:<x> slash form in a skill BODY (frontmatter descriptions may keep 'former /wicked-garden:x invocation' trigger phrases) — skills are not slash commands on any CLI

a line-leading `VERDICT[:=]` line in any skills/**/*.md (fenced blocks included — the contract templates live in fences) must be exactly `VERDICT: PASS`, `VERDICT: FAIL` or the template `VERDICT: PASS|FAIL`; CONDITIONAL / APPROVE / REJECT / SKIP are not verdicts; the legacy `VERDICT=… REVIEWER=… RUN_ID=…` footer is tolerated only in verdict_spelling.legacy_footer_files; nothing that is not line-leading is judged (`**VERDICT: …**`, a backticked mention, `### Verdict:`, a lowercase `verdict:` record line, a mid-line mention)

a SKILL.md whose frontmatter carries a top-level key outside the closed cross-CLI set {name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, mandates} — context, subagent_type, allowed-tools, model, effort, max-turns, color, user-invocable, phase_relevance, … are Claude Code plugin hints no other CLI reads; role/phases/archetypes move under `metadata:` (string→string), the rest are dropped

a body line that calls a Claude Code dispatch primitive — Task(, Skill(, Agent(, TaskCreate(, TaskUpdate(, TodoWrite(, subagent_type, AskUserQuestion — no other seat has them; a `<!-- historical -->` line is exempt; for the framework-ambiguous nouns `Task(` / `Agent(` ONLY, an assignment / constructor / lambda context (`x = Agent(`, `new Agent({`, `lambda: Agent(`) is framework code in a sample, not a dispatch (B8, the agentic domain's CrewAI / AutoGen / ADK samples) — `Skill(`, `TaskCreate(`, `TaskUpdate(`, `TodoWrite(` trip in every context (BC-38: the lint fails any skill on `Skill(`); the cross-CLI shape is a Hand-off paragraph naming the skill

Claude-only prose — a tool noun (`the Read tool`, `the Skill tool`, …), a `.claude/` path or the words `Claude Code` — outside a Hand-off paragraph and not marked `<!-- historical -->`; matched over the PARAGRAPH with intra-paragraph newlines normalised to spaces, so a token split across a line wrap (`multiple Bash` / `tool calls`) cannot hide from the line-based scan (review-garden-1158 M1)
a file that dispatches (any claude-dispatch hit) but carries no `Hand-off` paragraph — the only cross-CLI dispatch shape

a body line naming a retired product (wicked-testing, wicked-brain, wicked-signals, wicked-loom) without `<!-- historical -->` — the batches rewrite them to their successors (qe domain / wicked-estate / the in-process gate)
a SKILL.md frontmatter description longer than 1024 characters — several CLIs truncate or refuse it
a SKILL.md over 500 lines or 24 KiB — move detail into refs/ (the same bound scripts/ci/validate.py enforces for routers)

a body line that calls a Claude Code tool — Read(, Write(, Edit(, MultiEdit(, Bash(, Glob(, Grep(, WebFetch(, WebSearch(, NotebookEdit( with an argument shape after the paren — no other seat has the call; say what to do with your harness's file reader / shell / file search instead; a `<!-- historical -->` line is exempt (review-garden-1153 M1: the class was lint-blind for two batches)
